title: Bounded submission to a thread pool
summary: Stream results in input order while capping how many tasks have been submitted ahead of the consumer.
triggers: bounded submission and backpressure for a thread pool
an input stream can overwhelm the executor backlog
prompts: Process a long stream of files with a fixed amount of work ahead of the consumer while preserving input order.
Stop reading after the first result and cancel work from this batch that has yet to start.
invariant: At most limit jobs have been submitted without yielding their result. Each new submission follows a result the caller has pulled.
mantra: Fill a window, yield one, refill one.
pitfalls: A worker limit caps active threads. Submission also needs a cap if the producer can outrun the pool.
The limit applies to one iterator. Several callers sharing a pool need a shared admission limit.
Waiting for the oldest future can hold up faster results behind it. Completion order can help if callers do not need input order.
Close the iterator on early exit, for example with contextlib.closing. Cancellation can prevent queued tasks from starting while running calls continue.

mutations.explanation: Eagerly consuming the input creates a future for every item before yielding a result.

test: results = bounded_map(pool, lambda value: value ** 2, inputs(), limit=2)
